checklist_compliance.notes: Checklist derived from the change's own security intent (INVARIANTS.md self-protection threat model): (1) fix closes the false-allow — VERIFIED empirically; (2) no code injection via env path — VERIFIED; (3) env var names do not leak/collide — VERIFIED; (4) no secrets/privilege surface in diff — VERIFIED.

detail: T1 false-allow of guard weakening (removal of deny()/exit 2 masked by corrupted NEW_CONTENT) — MITIGATED by F49 (ENVIRON[] preserves literal bytes; verified pre-fix=ALLOW, post-fix=DENY)
T2 awk-program code injection via attacker-controlled old_string/new_string — NOT PRESENT (values read via ENVIRON[] at runtime, never interpolated into program text; system() payload proven inert)
T3 environment-variable leakage/collision (__IG_OLD__/__IG_NEW__) — NOT PRESENT (local + command-prefix scoping; proven unset in caller after return; inherited env of same name is overridden)

findings.issue: Residual fail-OPEN in apply_replace() awk-failure fallback: `2>/dev/null || printf '%s' "$1"` returns the ORIGINAL content on any non-zero awk exit, so downstream weakening checks compare file-vs-file and detect no change (ALLOW). F49 removes the dominant trigger (multi-line/backslash old_strings no longer fatal awk errors via ENVIRON), leaving only awk-absent / E2BIG / OOM. E2BIG is unreachable for protected files (max 18.9KB vs ARG_MAX 1,048,576). Recommend making the fallback fail-CLOSED (emit sentinel forcing deny) to match the hook's documented jq-absence fail-closed canon (lines 68-85). Pre-existing; not introduced by F49.

No has_awk presence guard mirroring has_jq. The guard relies on awk in ~10 places (apply_replace, deny_has_exit, count_array, INV-3 numeric compare, INV-7 line-shrink), each with `2>/dev/null || echo 0 / || true` fallbacks. On a host without awk, ALL awk-based weakening checks degrade to 'no weakening' = systemic fail-OPEN, inconsistent with the jq-absence path which fails closed for protected files. Recommend a has_awk fail-closed gate. Pre-existing; not introduced by F49.

Root-cause note is slightly incomplete: for the codebase's dominant case (multi-line old_strings with embedded newlines), onetrueawk `-v` fails with a FATAL 'awk: newline in string' error (non-zero exit) routed through the `|| printf` fallback — not merely silent backslash-dropping. The ENVIRON fix correctly covers BOTH failure modes, so there is no code defect; documentation-accuracy nit only.

fix_verification.evidence: Sourced pre-fix (`-v o=/n=`) and post-fix (ENVIRON[]) apply_replace with a backslash-newline old_string that removes an `exit 2` line, then ran the guard's real count (`grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*exit 2[[:space:]]*$'`). PRE-FIX: exit-2 count preserved (1) -> guard verdict ALLOW (false-allow). POST-FIX: exit-2 count -> 0 -> guard verdict DENY. ENVIRON length(old_string)=44 (correct) vs `-v` fatal 'newline in string'. Injection payload inserted as literal bytes (no system() exec). Caller-scope __IG_OLD__/__IG_NEW__ = unset after return.
fix_verification.regression_tests: tests/invariant-guard.bats +4 tests including 'apply_replace reflects deny()/exit-2 removal instead of silently returning unchanged content (false-allow prevention)'; asserted red-before/green-after by commit; bats 515/515.
